findings.statement: Theorem 1G: a mixed rule with grouped paid blocks that is separated (every paid rank below every job size) costs at most C n^tau (ln n)^kappa in the job model, with tau the root of its balance, kappa = ceil(ln(2/eta_m)/ln(1/theta)), theta = ln r_max/ln k_min; so every saving below 1 - tau is reached with a fixed constant. The construction is a dilated lockstep tree: exactly balanced, integral, deadlock-free, with exits done by fresh calls.
findings.status_detail: two independent AI skeptics re-derived and simulated it (one re-derived the logic with its own simulation, one built the construction explicitly with a generic deadlock test) and found no error; no person and no proof checker has read it

findings.statement: Lemma A (the exact condition for the top-split induction with leftovers) and Lemma A4: a flow whose leftovers carry all the Phi can never give exact O(n^tau) through this induction; so exact O(n^tau) without a log factor is not reached by this construction for grouped blocks.
findings.status_detail: part of the Theorem 1G proof; both skeptics' hypothesis checks agree with A4 at every n tested

findings.statement: Every numerical check of the construction holds: 0 unbalanced points, sources in (L/m, L], Phi(exits) = Phi(sources), exits within r_max (L/m)^theta, the unit bound, a cost T(n)/n^tau that grows far below (ln n)^kappa (flat for the rank-1 control), and hypothesis (E) of Lemma A3 at every n up to 12,800 for five test rules and, for the T74 what-if rule, at every n up to 20,000 and at every 997th n up to 3,000,000.
findings.status_detail: exact computations by the proof's own programs and by two skeptics' independent programs; all re-run on 19 Oct 2026 for this revision with identical outputs
